world_scale.nominal_ratio: 1:40 for vehicles and characters; trees and cliffs are compressed (diorama style) so the 1.2 m disk still reads as a forest
world_scale.note: target_size_m values are what the prefab should measure in Unity world units after import. Reconcile with the gameplay code (Assets/LastLight/Scripts) if it defines different lane or disk dimensions; the gameplay values win.

style.prompt_suffix: stylized 3D miniature diorama game asset, crisp clean shapes, chunky readable silhouette, slightly exaggerated proportions, hand-painted matte textures, muted midnight pine green and charcoal palette, single isolated object, no ground, no base
style.negative_base: photorealistic, photo scan, noisy detail, text, logo, watermark, ground plane, base plate, pedestal, multiple objects, blurry texture, glossy plastic

pricing.source: https://developers.tripo3d.ai/en/pricing and tripo docs --topic commands/generate (tripo-cli 0.8.0), checked 2026-10-28. 1 credit = 0.01 USD. List prices; the CLI plan card / dry run is authoritative for the generation step.

unity.replaces_placeholder: zombie capsule primitive in the horde
unity.rig_import: Animation Type Humanoid, Avatar created from this model; clips from LL_Zombie_A@walk.fbx and LL_Zombie_A@run.fbx (Loop Time on, Root Transform baked)

assets.notes: Optional polish: the playable disk top must be procedural (see island_disk_top).

Build procedurally in Unity: the top surface and road are scrolling chunk meshes clipped/masked to the 1.2 m circle, with exact three-lane geometry and a dark rim band. Tripo cannot produce exact lane widths or tileable scrolling chunks.

Procedural: thin rounded cylinder or ring with an emissive rim (muted coral when active). Must match the interaction volume exactly, so author it in Unity.
Procedural: emissive amber sphere or diamond with an acid green ghost-path line renderer for the lane preview.
